title: Evoloop: sheathed self-replicating CA loops whose size mutates in collisions and breeds true; on 3 of 3 seeds successive sweeps replace the side-11 founders by faster-breeding small kinds, with deaths by intrinsic dissolution
summary: Sayama's evoloop (9-state von Neumann CA, Golly table Evoloop.rule) founded by two planted Langton-type loops of hole side 11 (90 degrees apart, seed-dependent positions) on a 400^2 torus, run 200k steps with a loop-level genealogy (evo_track.py: every loop is its enclosed hole, followed every 20 steps; births with parent, deaths, kind changes; kind = hole side). Loops copy their genome into same-size daughters (labkit packs, seeds 1-2 at 300^2 and 20k steps: 218-224 persistent splits, max generation 27-28, merge/split 0.40); 38k-159k births per run, every loop dies by dissolution (state 8), and collisions make off-size daughters. Kinds that sweep breed true (side 11: 0.67-0.72, side 12: 0.69-0.73, side 4: 0.81, side 3: 0.85-0.90) with 0.05-0.09 kind changes of living loops per off-kind birth. Small kinds breed about twice as fast per loop-time (births per 1000 loop-steps: side 11 about 2.0, side 4 about 4.1, side 3 4.3-4.8) and replace the founders on 3 of 3 seeds (side 4 at t~85k on seed 2, then side 3; side 4 at t~185k on seed 3; side 3/2 at t~190k on seed 1 after a side-12 phase), as in the single-founder sighting. Variation control: the SDSR rule (same loops and dissolution, no evolution rules) from side-8 founders keeps side 4 at 92% breed-true with non-viable variants (about 0.03 offspring each) for 100k steps on 2 seeds. Limits: S fails (planted founders; 27 random soups freeze into debris), no identical-event neutral twin, B is written by the rule, and the side-12 takeover on seed 1 goes against the birth-rate ordering.

claims.statement: From planted founders, evoloop loops (a sheath ring around a core ring that carries the genome) reproduce through 27+ generations, die only by intrinsic structural dissolution, vary in size through collision-damaged copies, breed true by kind, and on 3 of 3 seeds faster-breeding small kinds that arose during the run displace the founders' kind through births and deaths.
claims.track: seed 2 (tracker run trk2_s2, world.py seed 2 at 400^2): the side-3 loops after t=150k (birthstrip_s2.png rows 1, 3-6, side 3->3 births): each is a sheathed loop (B) born of a side-3 parent beside it (D), in the side-3 kind that arose from side-4 parents and swept to 317 of 334 loops by t=200k (kinds.png panel 2; demography.json trk2_s2 kind 3: breed-true 0.85, 4.82 births per 1000 loop-steps vs 1.97 for the founders' side 11)

controls_run.H: variation control, not a neutral twin: censuses.json/demography.json sdsr8_s1 and sdsr8_s2 (SDSR-Loop.rule, same side-8 founders and dissolution, no evolution rules): side 4 holds 240-254 of 247-260 loops for 100k steps, off-size daughters are non-viable (0.02-0.03 offspring each, breed-true <= 0.04); Evoloop with the same side-8 founders is evo8_s1. Per-kind births, deaths, kind changes of living loops and off-kind daughters are in demography.json for all 6 runs
controls_run.B: ablation/sheath_s1.json, sheath_s2.json: removing a mature side-11 loop's sheath (state 2) dissolves it within 300 steps in 16/16 loops whose untouched twin survives; ablation/core_s1.json, core_s2.json: removing only 8 core cells does the same (16/16), so the sheath is a differentiated part but not uniquely load-bearing
controls_run.D: pack/seed1, pack/seed2: labkit lineage with K=3 frames (300 steps; loops live about 200-700 steps): 224 and 218 persistent splits, max generation 27 and 28, merge/split 0.40

claims.bd_control: not applicable: a discrete cellular automaton has no Laplacian operator to swap; the matched control is the SDSR rule (variation off)
